question.worked_solution:
The integral is defined over a type I region.

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{2-x}2y\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{2-x}2y\,dy]\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{y}^{2}]_{{x}^{2}}^{2-x}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}((2-x)^{2}-{x}^{4})\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(-{x}^{4}+{x}^{2}-4x+4)\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}(-{x}^{4}+{x}^{2}-4x+4)\,dx & =-{[\frac{{x}^{5}}{5}+\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}-2{x}^{2}+4x]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{3}-2+4-0 \\  & =\frac{32}{15}\end{aligned}
$$
